ekranHook: Its not the fire that kills

pencereler.0-5: An explosion does not kill mainly with fire. It kills with pressure - a
pencereler.5-12: wall of air moving faster than sound. In a fraction of a second, solid material turns into expanding gas.
pencereler.12-20: That gas slams outward as a shockwave, crushing everything near it. The wave can burst lungs and eardrums before the heat even
pencereler.20-30: arrives. Then comes the vacuum, as air rushes back to fill the gap. That reverse pull can suck windows and debris back toward the blast. Distance is everything

segmentler.metin: An explosion does not kill mainly with fire.
It took only solid material turning into gas.
The answer is blast overpressure — and it is why blast engineers design with distance first.
